data.title: DCSync - Replication of Domain Credentials
data.summary: An account with directory replication rights was used to request the password hashes of all domain accounts directly from a domain controller, including the krbtgt account, without executing code on the DC itself.
data.description:
Active Directory domain controllers replicate credential data between each other using the Directory Replication Service Remote Protocol (MS-DRSR). Any security principal holding the Replicating Directory Changes and Replicating Directory Changes All extended rights on the domain object can invoke this protocol to request password data for any account.

Members of Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, and the domain controller computer accounts hold these rights by default. When an attacker compromises an account with these privileges, or when the rights have been delegated to a non-administrative account through misconfiguration, the attacker can replicate the NTLM hash and Kerberos keys of every account in the domain.

The attack was performed using secretsdump.py (Impacket) or the lsadump::dcsync module in mimikatz. The replication request is handled by the domain controller as a normal replication operation and does not require code execution on the DC, file access to NTDS.dit, or physical proximity to the server.

Recovery of the krbtgt hash allows the creation of Golden Tickets, granting persistent domain-wide access that survives password resets for all accounts except krbtgt itself. The krbtgt password must be reset twice (due to password history) to invalidate forged tickets.

Replication traffic from a non-DC source is a reliable indicator of this attack but is not monitored by default.
data.impact: The attacker obtained the password hash of every account in the domain, including all administrative, service, and user accounts. This grants the ability to authenticate as any user, forge Kerberos tickets for persistent access, and extract sensitive data protected by domain credentials. Recovery requires resetting the krbtgt account password twice and rotating all account credentials.
data.recommendation:
1. Remove replication rights from all accounts that are not domain controllers. Audit the domain object ACL for non-default entries holding Replicating Directory Changes or Replicating Directory Changes All.

2. Restrict Domain Admin membership to the minimum required accounts and treat every member as a tier-zero asset.

3. Deploy monitoring for replication requests originating from non-domain-controller sources. Event ID 4662 with the replication GUIDs identifies this activity.

4. Reset the krbtgt account password twice in succession to invalidate any Golden Tickets that may have been created, following Microsoft guidance for the reset interval.

5. Implement a tiered administration model so that accounts with replication rights are used only from hardened, dedicated administrative workstations.

6. Review all accounts compromised during this assessment and force credential rotation for every domain account, as the attacker held the ability to authenticate as any of them.
